articles.title: 民主主義は「尊重される経験」から芽生える。韓国・社会的協同組合Partiがつくる、市民のためのデジタル空間
articles.summary:
自らの声が尊重されることを「実感したこと」があるか──この実感を重視するのが、韓国の社会的協同組合Parti。デジタル技術で「日常の民主主義」を取り戻すべく、行政への政策提言から相反する意見の市民による対話まで、市民が主役となる広場をデジタル技術を軸に創り出しています。さらに、Partiそのものが協同組合という組織体を選ぶことで、互いを尊重できる社会に向けたガバナンスの形を示すという考え方に迫ります。
The post 民主主義は「尊重される経験」から芽生える。韓国・社会的協同組合Partiがつくる、市民のためのデジタル空間 first appeared on IDEAS FOR GOOD.

articles.title: 「ここが私の畳」気軽な“関与”で文化財を守り継ぐ、柳川・SAMURAI REBIRTHの古畳循環プロジェクト
articles.summary:
福岡県柳川市の「柳川藩主立花邸 御花」では、倉庫に眠っていた古い畳と、これまで焼却していた庭園の落ち葉を使って、堆肥をつくる取り組みを2023年から始めています。堆肥はい草畑に撒かれ、育ったい草は新しい畳になり、大広間へと戻される。前例のない循環の仕組みです。
2年3ヶ月で活用した古畳は30枚、再生畳として大広間に戻された枚数は80枚。この畳一枚ずつを支援する「一口畳主（Joshu）」という制度には、すでに約80人が参加。文化財を「見る対象」から「関わる対象」に変えていくための、具体的な仕組みについて話を聞きました。

articles.title: MIT’s tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
articles.summary: A new AI control system lets MIT’s tiny flying robot move with insect-like agility, boosting its speed by about 450 percent and allowing it to pull off 10 somersaults in 11 seconds. articles.title: Brain scans reveal a possible cause of long COVID fatigue and brain fog
articles.summary: Researchers have found evidence that long COVID may damage dopamine releasing neurons in the brain, potentially explaining persistent fatigue, low motivation, slowed movement, and memory difficulties. The discovery could lead to new treatments that target the brain's dopamine system.

articles.summary: Scientists have found that the human brain develops from two distinct cellular systems, suggesting that evolution fused together two ancient nervous systems with very different jobs. articles.title: Hurricane Hunters reveal 4 warning signs that a storm is about to strengthen
articles.summary: Nearly three decades of Hurricane Hunter data reveal four features that can help a tilted tropical cyclone straighten its circulation and become capable of intensifying. The findings could give forecasters an earlier warning that a seemingly disorganized storm is becoming primed to strengthen.

articles.title: New nanoparticles make hidden chemical differences light up
articles.summary: Scientists have developed ultra-bright nanoparticles that can detect tiny amounts of chemicals and distinguish between molecules that look almost identical. The technology could one day provide a cheaper way to catch dangerous drug impurities or trace pollutants using simple low-cost lasers.

articles.title: Ancient DNA reveals how plague kept returning for 400 years after the Black Death

articles.title: A 66-million-year-old tooth reveals T. rex was nearly as warm as a human
articles.summary: Chemical clues preserved inside fossilized T. rex teeth reveal that the dinosaur maintained a body temperature of about 97 degrees Fahrenheit, almost identical to humans. articles.title: Caltech’s tiny new chip can steer light in 74 quadrillionths of a second
articles.summary: A new Caltech device can redirect a beam of light in just 74 femtoseconds using another beam and a nanoscale silicon metasurface. The breakthrough could pave the way for dramatically faster photonic communications, computing, and sensing technologies.

articles.summary: A 150-million-year-old dinosaur fossil from Spain has been identified as the first confirmed Diplodocus ever found outside North America. articles.title: Ozempic can change your body. Can it change your life?
articles.summary: Ozempic and other GLP-1 medications can improve blood sugar, weight, and cardiovascular health, but researchers found little evidence that they also improve mental health, employment, marriage, or overall well-being. articles.title: A $100 detector can see invisible particles raining down from space
articles.summary: A pocket-sized, roughly $100 detector can reveal the invisible stream of cosmic particles constantly passing through Earth and even through our bodies. What began as a student physics project is now being used in major experiments, balloon missions, and potentially future spacecraft.
